originality.rationale: A full-text published-finding corpus comparison shows the finite cross-covariance is covered by a direct sum of its exact richness-versus-every-frequency formula. It is not assessed as original. The narrower two-scale normalized-correlation law adds the parity variance and explicit triangular-array limits for t/n and t/(n log n), which are not stated or implied as standalone results by that earlier covariance formula alone. Originality remains qualified by possible older normalization results.
residual_risks: An earlier exact equal-probability occupancy-versus-parity covariance may exist under alternative terminology; negative search is not uniqueness proof.
General multinomial moment identities may imply the finite formulas as a specialization; the two-scale profile is an additional analysis, not independent from those identities.
The full Diaconis–Graham–Morrison and Muratov–Zuyev articles were not inspected; no assertion of full-text noncoverage is made.
The full published-finding corpus manuscripts for nearest two summaries were not read; their summaries do not imply the joint sign and scaling profile.

The narrow normalized-correlation limits can be derived from standard parity variance plus the existing all-frequency covariance, so their value depends on the intrinsic interest of the explicit dependence crossover; no broad novelty from the numerator is claimed.

value.rationale: The contribution assessed is the explicit normalized-correlation profile between exploration and current displacement at linear times and the polynomial decorrelation exponent on n log n times, not the finite cross-covariance numerator (already implied by prior full-frequency formulas). These two simultaneous scaling laws quantify a natural joint statistic of a high-dimensional walk across nontrivially different time scales and make a precise benchmark for future multivariate approximations.
